title: `gh release create` does not recognise GitHub Enterprise Cloud (ghe.com) remotes when using `GH_TOKEN`

labels.name: priority-2
labels.description: Affects more than a few users but doesn't prevent core functions

body:
### Describe the bug

After migrating from GitHub.com to GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency (`<tenant>.ghe.com`), an existing GitHub Actions release workflow fails because `gh` does not recognise the repository's remote as a known GitHub host.

The workflow supplies `GH_TOKEN` using `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`:

```yaml
- name: Create GitHub Release
  env:
    GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
  run: gh release create "${TAG}" --generate-notes
```

 The checkout's remote points to `https://<tenant>.ghe.com/<owner>/<repo>`, but `gh release create` asks me to run `gh auth login`.

Explicitly setting the repository fixes the problem:

```yaml
env:
  GH_REPO: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}
```

### Affected version

`gh version 2.98.0 (2026-08-20)`

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Use a repository on GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency (`<tenant>.ghe.com`).
2. Run the following workflow by pushing a version tag.
3. Observe that the `gh release create` step fails.

```yaml
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+"

permissions: {}

jobs:
  gh-release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    permissions:
      contents: write

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Create GitHub Release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: gh release create "${TAG}" --generate-notes
```

### Expected vs actual behavior

Expected: `gh` recognises the `*.ghe.com` remote as a GitHub host, infers the repository from the checkout, and creates the release using `GH_TOKEN`, without requiring `GH_HOST`, `GH_REPO`, or an interactive login.

Actual: remote resolution fails with the error below. The same workflow worked on GitHub.com, and explicitly setting `GH_REPO` makes it work on the data-residency instance.

### Logs

```text
none of the git remotes configured for this repository point to a known GitHub host. To tell gh about a new GitHub host, please use `gh auth login`
```
